catalyst_text_evidence: In MTAP-deleted tumors, this biology establishes a robust synthetic lethal vulnerability that underpins the mechanistic rationale for combining IDE892 and IDE397, where the first-patient-in (FPI) was achieved in mid-2026. IDE892 and IDE397 combination escalation are ongoing in MTAP NSCLC and PDAC, and IDE892 and pan-RAS combination FPI in MTAP PDAC is targeted for H2 2026.

catalyst_text: Announced significant PFS benefit and RTOR acceptance
detailed_catalyst_text: Presented complete primary analysis data from a registrational Phase 2/3 trial in first-line HLA-A2:01 negative metastatic uveal melanoma showing a statistically significant PFS improvement versus investigator’s choice and higher ORR/DCR with manageable safety. The trial met its primary endpoint by BICR, with median PFS of 6.9 months vs. 3.1 months. Separately, the FDA agreed to review the NDA under the RTOR program, and the first pre-submission was completed.
catalyst_text_evidence: IDEAYA Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:IDYA), a leading precision medicine oncology company, and Servier, an independent international pharmaceutical group governed by a foundation, today presented complete data from the primary analysis of their registrational Phase 2/3 OptimUM-02 trial of darovasertib in combination with crizotinib (darovasertib combination) in first line (1L) HLA*A2:01 negative metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM) at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting taking place in Chicago, Illinois. The trial met the primary endpoint, with patients treated with the darovasertib combination demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in median PFS of 6.9 months versus 3.1 months in the ICT arm by BICR (HR: 0.42; 95% CI: 0.30, 0.59; p-value: <0.0001). In April 2026, IDEAYA announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has agreed to review their new drug application (NDA) for darovasertib in combination with crizotinib under the Oncology Center of Excellence Real-time Oncology Review (RTOR) program. IDEAYA completed its first pre-submission in May and expects to complete the NDA filing in the second half of 2026.

catalyst_text: Accepted into FDA RTOR program after positive data
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA agreed to review an NDA for the combination therapy under the Real-Time Oncology Review program, reflecting regulatory engagement based on existing data. Positive topline Phase 2/3 results in first-line HLA*A2-negative metastatic uveal melanoma showed the study met its primary endpoint with significant PFS benefit and notable response rate. This supports potential expedited review for a population with limited options.
catalyst_text_evidence: IDEAYA Biosciences, Inc. today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has agreed to review its New Drug Application (NDA) for darovasertib in combination with crizotinib (darovasertib combination) for patients with first line (1L) HLA*A2-negative metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM) under the Oncology Center of Excellence (OCE) Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) program. On 2026-04-13, IDEAYA reported positive topline data from the Phase 2/3 OptimUM-02 trial of darovasertib in combination with crizotinib in 1L HLA*A2-negative mUM. The trial met its primary endpoint, with the combination reducing the risk of disease progression by 58% (Hazard Ratio of 0.42; 95% CI: 0.30, 0.59; p-value: <0.0001) and achieving a statistically significant improvement in median progression-free survival (PFS) of 6.9 months versus 3.1 months in the investigator choice of therapy (ICT) arm as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). On secondary endpoints, an overall response rate (ORR) of 37.1%, including 5 complete responses, was observed in patients treated with the darovasertib combination versus 5.8% in the ICT arm (p-value: <0.0001) with a median duration of response (DOR) of 6.8 months.

catalyst_text: Trial met primary endpoint with significant PFS improvement
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results from the randomized registrational Phase 2/3 OptimUM-02 study in first-line HLA-A*02:01-negative metastatic uveal melanoma showed a statistically significant PFS benefit versus investigator’s choice by BICR (HR 0.42; median 6.9 vs 3.1 months). ORR by BICR was 37.1% versus 5.8%, including five complete responses, with a manageable safety profile.
catalyst_text_evidence: IDEAYA Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:IDYA), a precision medicine oncology company, and Servier, an independent international pharmaceutical group governed by a foundation, today announced positive topline results from their Phase 2/3 registrational trial, OptimUM-02, evaluating darovasertib in combination with crizotinib (darovasertib combination) in patients with first-line (1L) HLA-A*A2:01-negative metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM). The darovasertib combination met the trial's primary endpoint of a statistically significant improvement in median progression-free survival (PFS) relative to the investigator choice of therapy (ICT) arm as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). Patients treated with the darovasertib combination reduced their risk of disease progression as assessed by BICR by 58% (Hazard Ratio of 0.42; 95% CI: 0.30, 0.59; p-value: <0.0001) and achieved a statistically significant improvement in median PFS of 6.9 months versus 3.1 months in the ICT arm. The overall response rate (ORR) by BICR in the darovasertib combination and ICT arm was 37.1% and 5.8% (p-value: <0.0001), respectively. There were 5 complete responses by BICR observed in the darovasertib combination arm, and no complete responses observed in the ICT arm.

catalyst_text_evidence: IDEAYA Biosciences, Inc. catalyst_text_evidence: IDEAYA Biosciences, Inc. ... announced first-patient-in for a Phase 1 clinical trial combination study to evaluate IDE849, a potential first-in-class delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3)-targeting Topo-I-payload antibody drug conjugate (ADC) program, and IDE161, a potential first-in-class poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG) inhibitor. Announced successful FDA Type D meeting on Phase 3 trial design; Phase 3 neoadjuvant darovasertib trial in primary UM to begin in early 2025.

Initiated Phase 1/2 study expansion for IDE397, IDEAYA's MAT2A inhibitor, in combination with Trodelvy®, Gilead's Trop-2 directed ADC, in MTAP-deletion urothelial cancer based on preliminary safety and clinical efficacy data

The presentation of the Phase 1 trial at EORTC-NCI-AACR indicated a 33% overall response rate (ORR) according to RECIST 1.1, which included 1 complete response (CR) and 8 partial responses (PRs) from 27 evaluable patients with heavily pre-treated (median of 2-3 prior lines, ranging from 1 to 7) MTAP-deletion urothelial carcinoma (UC) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSC).

The efficacy data from Phase 2 indicated that 49% of patients experienced more than 30% reduction in tumor size based on the product of diameters, along with a 61% rate of eye preservation among patients who underwent enucleation, as reported on September 23, 2024.
The update for Phase 2 data indicated an Overall Response Rate (ORR) of 39%. This includes one (1) complete response and six (6) partial responses, as reported on July 8, 2024.

Further information presented at ASCO indicated that 75% (9 of 12 enucleation patients) had verified Eye Saved, and around 67% (8 of 12 enucleation patients) experienced more than 30% tumor reduction.

Data from Phase 1 indicated that tumor reduction was noted in several patients with HRD solid tumors, which included a patient with endometrial cancer who showed a partial response in the initial imaging evaluation and an 87% decrease in size.

Data from Phase 2 involving the combination of darovasertib and crizotinib indicated a cORR of 45%, a DCR of 90%, and a median PFS of approximately 7 months among 20 evaluable patients with First-Line MUM, as reported on April 23, 2023.
